name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean of D+13
Incumbent Ed Case running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Adriel Lam has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at about 95%
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean, Case's incumbency and roughly $1.1 million raised against a little-known, unfunded Republican challenger make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, and markets agree at about 95%. With no polls available, uncertainty stays moderately wide, but nothing in the evidence points to a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Case underperforming his district lean, or unexpected outside spending for Lam, would be the first sign of trouble.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st District is a solidly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Ed Case is seeking another term and has raised roughly $1.1 million, holding about $600,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Adriel Lam, reports no fundraising, and minor-party candidates on the ballot lack resources as well.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 95 percent. The forecast expects Case to win comfortably, with a margin in the low twenties and modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
